enter verb

go or come into

also go in, come in, come in!, go inside, come inside, walk in, go inside!

classical

Phaedr. 5.9.2: cum vix intrāre posset ad praesēpia
Cic. Phil. 2.68: tū illud sānctissimum līmen intrāre? (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 310: enter, intrāre
Traupman 33: come in, intrā (intrāte)

intrō, intrāre, intrāvī, intrātum

adverb, conjugation

go in, come in, enter

Other words

  • intrō īre — go in, go inside

    the adverb intrō, in, inside, with a verb of motion · also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 1387: quīn intrō īs?; Plaut. Aul. 89: abī intrō

    Also written as one word, as in Terence’s intrōībās.

  • ingredior, ingredī, ingressus sum — step in, enter

    verb, third conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 2.68: tū ingredī illam domum ausus es? (Lewis & Short)

  • Ī intus! — go inside!

    avoid · modern · Traupman 101: ī (pl. īte) intus!; Traupman 333

    Intus is “inside”, of rest; with a verb of motion classical Latin says intrō: abī intrō (Plaut. Aul. 89). Lewis & Short notes intus for intrō as rare and doubtful, “cf. Quint. 1.5.50”, where it is cited as a fault. Say Ī intrō!.

Examples

  • Quis hīc loquitur? ehem, tūne hīc erās, mī Phaedria? Quid hīc stābās? cūr nōn rēctā intrōībās?

    who’s that talking? Oh, is it you, Phaedria dear? Why were you standing out here? Why didn’t you come straight in?Ter. Eun. 86–87

  • quid stās? quīn intrō īs?

    why are you standing there? Go on in!Plaut. Mil. 1387

  • angustō in aditū taurus luctāns cornibus cum vix intrāre posset ad praesēpia

    a bull, struggling with his horns in a narrow doorway, could hardly get in to his stallPhaedr. 5.9.1–2

  • abī intrō, occlūde jānuam. jam ego hīc erō.

    go in, shut the door, I’ll be right back.Plaut. Aul. 89

  • Intrā (intrāte).

    Come in.Traupman 33

See also inside, get in, go, door, enter.
